thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate (customer-facing). Canary rollout for model 'redwood-alpha-v2' started 30m ago. Current error rate: 12% over 5m window. Routing fallback observed. Paging eng-oncall.
carla (eng-oncall): got the page, joining. Pulling up dashboards. link: https://console.redwood/alerts/2191234567
alice (eng-runtime): I can see spike correlated with canary tokens hitting variant 'redwood-alpha-v2-q4' — errors show model init timeouts followed by sticky fallback to 'redwood-alpha-v1'.
bob (eng-sre): any region correlation? I see increased retries in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.
carla (eng-oncall): customers reporting higher latency + 5xxs. Elaine, can you confirm top affected tenants?
elaine (support): frank (CS) flagged 3 enterprise customers — checkout flow failed, visible 502s in their logs. I'll share request ids in thread.
frank (customer-success): customers seeing a lot of 'model variant mismatch' errors in app logs. They want ETA and mitigation.
alice (eng-runtime): digging into routing logs: rollout policy had canary fraction 10% but fallback policy sticky_affinity=true with no TTL. When the canary variant started failing, requests fell back to previous variant but sticky keys persisted, causing oscillation loops across regions.
derek (prod-reliability): that sticky affinity w/o TTL is dangerous during a rollout. Can we pause the canary and force immediate routing to stable?
bob (eng-sre): agree. Recommend pausing rollout and applying a routing override to send traffic to stable for affected customers.
carla (eng-oncall): action items: 1) pause canary, 2) disable sticky affinity for fallback, 3) short-circuit fallback to stable for high-error routes. Who can do each?
alice (eng-runtime): I can pause the canary now (runbook step). Executing: `redwood rollout pause --model redwood-alpha-v2 --env prod`
alice (eng-runtime): paused. Canary fraction -> 0%. Confirming in control plane.
carla (eng-oncall): great. Bob, can you disable sticky affinity? We need to avoid old sticky sessions sending requests into the loop.
bob (eng-sre): on it. Updating policy: `PATCH /policies/{smart-routing}` body: `{"fallback":{"sticky_affinity":false}}` Applying to prod region set.
bob (eng-sre): done. Waiting for propagation (~20s).
alice (eng-runtime): also rolling a forced override for the canary route to stable: `redwood route set --path /v1/generate --model redwood-alpha-v1 --scope affected-customers`
elain? (support): typo in command earlier from alice, support confirming which customers in scope.
elaine (support): applying to the flagged tenants from Frank. Notifying them: "we're routing you to the stable model while we investigate".
frank (customer-success): customers acknowledged and seeing immediate improvement in tail latency. Keeping them updated.
derek (prod-reliability): monitoring metrics — 5xx rate falling from 12% to 1.5% over 3 mins. Good.
carla (eng-oncall): are any worker nodes OOMing or failing health checks that explain canary init timeouts?
alice (eng-runtime): canary pods in us-west had repeated container restarts; logs show a libcuda init error on first warmup slice — could be a mismatched kernel or quantized config in alpha-v2-q4.
\obob? (eng-sre): typo — ignore.
bob (eng-sre): that's consistent with model variant binary incompatibility on some GPU drivers. We'll mark model variant as failing in model catalog.
derek (prod-reliability): next steps: 1) Revert canary artifacts from registry for v2-q4, 2) Block automatic retry rollouts, 3) Add TTL to sticky affinity to prevent future infinite fallback loops.
carla (eng-oncall): I'll file an incident ticket and assign owners. Alice, Bob, Derek — please include postmortem action items. Elaine/Frank, please update customers that mitigation is in place and we'll follow up.
incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by carla (eng-oncall). Incident severity set to sev2.
alice (eng-runtime): creating rollback MR to remove q4 variants and pin to v2-q2 for next canary attempts. Link: https://git.redwood/rollouts/1234
bob (eng-sre): adding a short-term policy patch: `sticky_affinity_ttl_seconds=300` for all rollouts; will scope later in config review.
frank (customer-success): customers appreciate quick response. They asked for root-cause writeup and ETA for safe re-rollout.
derek (prod-reliability): ETA for safe re-rollout: need kernel compatibility test (est 48h) + canary dry-run. We'll coordinate with infra.
carla (eng-oncall): summary for timeline and next messages: Incident opened 2191234567. Mitigation applied: canary paused, sticky affinity disabled, routing override to stable for affected tenants. Impact: several enterprise tenants saw 5xxs and latency spike — now reduced. Owners: alice (runtime) MR + rollback, bob (sre) policy patch, derek (prod-reliability) infra kernel check.\\ncarla (eng-oncall): will follow up with postmortem doc and severity review. If anyone spots regression — ping @carla. :white_check_mark:
